title: 2019 AMC 12B Problem 2
statement: Consider the statement, “If \(n\) is not prime, then \(n-2\) is prime.” Which of the following values of \(n\) is a counterexample to this statement?

solutions.text:
A counterexample needs \(n\) not prime (so the hypothesis holds) and \(n-2\) not prime (so the conclusion fails).

Among the choices, \(27\) is not prime and \(27-2=25\) is not prime. The primes \(11\) and \(19\) fail the hypothesis, and \(15-2=13,\) \(21-2=19\) are prime.

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: A counterexample makes the hypothesis true but the conclusion false
Look for \(n\) that is not prime while \(n-2\) is also not prime
